title: Cloud Production Design Decision Criteria
source: Weights and criteria derived from the Cloud, Server, and Production Deployment — Skill Catalog (Edition 1.0, November 2026) decision-matrix skill descriptions: availability, latency, residency, security, operational burden, recovery targets, scalability, lock-in, and total cost.

scale.note: Score every criterion 1 (worst) to 5 (best). For lower-better criteria, 5 means LOWEST burden/cost/lock-in.

criteria.name: Availability
criteria.description: Ability to meet the required SLO/SLA: multi-AZ/Region topology, managed failover, provider track record for the specific service class.

scoreGuide.1: Single point of failure; no SLA evidence.
scoreGuide.3: Multi-AZ with manual failover; standard SLA.
scoreGuide.5: Multi-AZ/Region, automated failover, strong SLA track record.

criteria.name: Latency
criteria.description: Network and service latency to the user population and to dependent systems (p95 at the edge and in-region).

scoreGuide.1: Far from users; no edge presence; chatty cross-region calls.
scoreGuide.3: Regional deployment with acceptable p95 for the workload.
scoreGuide.5: Edge/regional footprint; p95 comfortably within budget under peak.

criteria.name: Data Residency
criteria.description: Fit with data-residency and sovereignty requirements (where data is stored, processed, and logged; legal and contractual constraints).

scoreGuide.1: Violates or cannot evidence residency requirements.
scoreGuide.3: Meets requirements with region selection and contracts.
scoreGuide.5: Native residency fit incl. logs/backups/subprocessors; audit-ready evidence.

criteria.name: Security & Compliance
criteria.description: Isolation model, IAM maturity, encryption/KMS options, audit logging, compliance certifications relevant to the workload, WAF/abuse protection.

scoreGuide.1: Weak isolation; missing audit trail or certifications.
scoreGuide.3: Solid IAM/KMS/audit; certifications cover the workload.
scoreGuide.5: Defense-in-depth, short-lived credentials, proven compliance scope, mature incident tooling.

criteria.name: Operational Burden
criteria.description: Day-2 effort to run it: patching, capacity, upgrades, observability integration, toil. Score 5 when the burden is LOWEST.

scoreGuide.1: Heavy bespoke toil; scarce skills; manual every task.
scoreGuide.3: Managed where possible; known operational playbooks.
scoreGuide.5: Mostly serverless/managed; patching and scaling automated; minimal toil.

criteria.name: Recovery Targets (RPO/RTO)
criteria.description: Ability to meet documented RPO/RTO: replication, backup/restore speed, failover automation, drill evidence.

scoreGuide.1: Cannot meet targets or only via untested manual restores.
scoreGuide.3: Meets targets with planned failover and periodic drills.
scoreGuide.5: Meets aggressive targets with automated regional failover and measured drill evidence.

criteria.name: Scalability
criteria.description: Headroom to 10x without re-architecture: quotas, autoscaling, sharding model, downstream bottlenecks.

scoreGuide.1: Hard ceilings; re-architecture needed for growth.
scoreGuide.3: Scales with known limits and quota management.
scoreGuide.5: Elastic to 10x+ with headroom; quotas and sharding proven.

criteria.name: Portability / Lock-in
criteria.description: Cost of later migration: proprietary APIs, data egress fees, managed-service gravity. Score 5 when lock-in is LOWEST.

scoreGuide.3: Some coupling; portable data layer and IaC.
scoreGuide.5: Open standards, containers/Kubernetes, cheap egress, proven exit plan.

criteria.name: Total Cost of Ownership
criteria.description: 3-year TCO: infra + egress + licenses + ops headcount + compliance overhead. Score 5 when cost is LOWEST.

scoreGuide.3: Within budget with normal FinOps discipline.
scoreGuide.5: Cheapest credible option at required SLO; predictable growth.
